title: Melody/harmony 1
description: Practise the National 5 Melody/harmony concepts — collection 1 of 2.

items.prompt: Music with no established tonal centre and no functional major or minor key.
Name the general pitch adjective for movement by semitones, including notes outside the main key, rather than the name of a particular densely packed chord.
A dense chord made from adjacent or very closely spaced notes sounded together.
Two melodic parts move in opposite directions at the same time.
Name the general term for a distinct secondary melody heard alongside the main tune, rather than the specific high vocal part.
Name the specific high vocal part that decorates a main tune by singing an independent melody above it.
A pianist or harpist sweeps rapidly across consecutive notes between two pitches. Name this sliding run across the intervening notes.
Name the general term for a very short ornamental note immediately before a main note, rather than a repeated alternation of two notes.
A two-chord cadence ending on V. It sounds open or unfinished because chord I has not arrived.
A note sustained or repeatedly sounded in an upper part while the harmony beneath it changes.
